text:
San Jose arrives in Minnesota on a slide. The Sharks are 1-4-0 in their last five and winless in three, coming off a 7-2 loss at Los Angeles where Adrian Kempe scored three. Our numbers say the slump is real: they've had 40% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) in that stretch. They're without Igor Chernyshov and Alexander Wennberg, and Collin Graf and Mason Marchment have picked up the extra minutes. Minnesota is 4-0-1 in its last five, though it has been outchanced in most of those games, and it's missing Marcus Foligno, Nick Foligno and Jared Spurgeon.

The gap shows up everywhere. At five on five, the Wild have taken 54% of the expected goals against 44% for San Jose, and our model projects 3.95 goals for Minnesota to 2.63. Minnesota's power play creates 0.91 expected goals a game, and the Sharks' penalty kill allows 0.92, while San Jose takes 4.1 penalties a game. In net, projected starter Jesper Wallstedt is +12.2 in goals saved above expected (how many goals a goalie has stopped beyond what the shots should have yielded), and he's +5.8 over 35 games last season. Yaroslav Askarov is +4.7 this year but was -19.4 last season.

Kirill Kaprizov is our top pick, at 55% to score, on a six-game point streak, and Matt Boldy sits at 47% with his own six-game streak. For San Jose, Macklin Celebrini is 36% to score, and Mason Marchment is a goal shy of 100 for his career. Among our under-the-radar picks, Michael McCarron is a third-line depth scorer at 14% to score, and Maxim Shabanov, newly in the top six, is 50% for a point. Both are players to watch.
